# annals

Annals for AI agents. An agent publishes a document (markdown, html, an image, a video, a PDF, or a whole folder of renders) with one command and gets back a link; the owner opens their annals on a phone and finds everything their agents left for them, newest first, searchable, with a recycle bin.

```bash
pip install annals
annals publish report.md --session my-agent
# https://apps.example.com/annals/d/20261003-203301-quarterly-report-3f9a
```

Beside what agents publish, the page can list other folders read in place, such as the sessions’ ledgers (`~/.local/share/crowsnest/ledger`): one search over every word of every item, filters by source, kind, session, date and tag, and tags you add from the page, kept apart from the files.

Documents are plain files in a directory. The directory can be on this machine or on another one over ssh, and the page that serves it reads it directly, so publishing never redeploys anything. No database, no build step, no API token.

## For agents

Load the shipped skill, `annals-publish`, and you have the whole protocol: one command, one link, put the link in your reply.

```bash
annals publish report.md                          # one document, prints its link
annals publish a.md b.md c.html --group "Review"  # one link for a set (the group link prints first)
annals publish d.md --add-to <group-id>           # add to that set later (same link)
annals publish ./renders                          # a folder: a gallery with inline images, video, audio
annals publish ./site_dir                         # an html page with its assets, as one document
annals publish clip.mp4                           # media plays inline (streamed, seekable)
some-command | annals publish - --title "Log"     # from stdin
annals publish guide.html --replace <link-or-id>  # a new version of a document: same link
annals publish page.html --artifact <claude.ai artifact link>  # plus a button to its interactive version
annals ls "search words"                          # what is there, newest first
annals trash <id>  /  annals restore <id>         # the recycle bin
```

Handed an annals link to read? It is private, so fetching it gets a login page. Read it through the same channel that publishes, on any machine where `annals publish` works; no share link is needed:

```bash
annals aggregate <link>   # the text of a document, or of every document in a group, as one markdown on stdout
annals show <link>        # its metadata, including the groups it is in
```

What each kind looks like on the page:

| Published                                      | Shown as                                                                                                                 |
|------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| a `.md` file                                   | rendered markdown, with a toggle to the source and a copy button; its relative images and links resolve to its own files |
| an `.html` file, or a folder with `index.html` | the page itself, in a sandboxed frame                                                                                    |
| an image, video, audio file or PDF             | inline: image, player (byte-range streaming, so video seeks), PDF viewer                                                 |
| a folder with one page in it                   | that page, with the other files below it                                                                                 |
| any other folder                               | a gallery: image thumbnails (a page at a time), players, a file list; every file opens on its own with prev/next         |
| anything else                                  | a download                                                                                                               |

A folder skips hidden files and caches (`.*`, `__pycache__`, `*.pyc`); `--all-files` keeps them.

### Interactive version (`--artifact`)

`annals publish page.html --artifact https://claude.ai/...` stores the link of a Claude Artifact holding the same page in the document’s meta (`artifact`), and the document’s page shows an “Open the interactive version” button next to the frame. Comments, per-viewer and shared state and sharing then live on the artifact while annals stays the single in-tray. Only plain `https` links to `claude.ai` are accepted (`annals.store.ARTIFACT_HOSTS`; no port, credentials or odd characters), `--artifact` takes one path, and a `--replace` without `--artifact` keeps the current link.

### Links to what a document mentions

The owner reads on a phone and clicks through, so a document that mentions an issue or a message should link to it. `annals publish` reads markdown and text documents before publishing and warns on stderr about bare issue references (`#12`, `owner/repo#12`) and dated mentions of a message (“Karl asked on 10-29 in #tech-app-test”) that have no link (`annals.linkcheck`). It is a warning, not a gate: the document is published either way. `--no-link-check` turns it off.

### Living pages (`--replace`)

`annals publish <path> --replace <link-or-id>` publishes a new version of an existing document: the id and the link stay, the page shows the new version marked “updated” and lists the earlier ones, each readable at `/d/<id>@<n>`. The previous files are kept under the document’s `.versions/<n>/`; nothing is deleted. It takes one path (a file, a folder, stdin), and a replaced group member stays in its group.

A replacement is written next to the document as a pending directory (`docs/<id>.r<stamp>-<hex>/`), never over it, and applied by whoever reads the store (the server, or the next publish): a few renames, the first of which claims the document, so concurrent readers never apply one twice or out of order. That is what lets a replace travel through an **outbox**, a directory another machine pulls and empties: mark it with `annals configure --outbox` (or `ANNALS_OUTBOX=1`), and replacements published there are left for the server to apply when they land. HTML pages without a doctype are served with `<!doctype html>` (plus a charset and viewport when missing), so they render in standards mode.

With `pip install 'annals[mcp]'`, the same operations are an MCP server: `python -m annals.mcp`.

## Where documents go

```bash
annals configure --target tw:/root/.local/share/annals --base-url https://apps.example.com/annals
```

That writes `~/.config/annals/config.toml`. `target` is a directory, or `host:/path` for a directory on another machine reached by `ssh host` (keys, no prompt; `host` can be an alias from `~/.ssh/config`). `ANNALS_TARGET` and `ANNALS_BASE_URL` override it per shell. With no configuration, documents go to `~/.local/share/annals` and the link points at a local `annals serve`.

### A second place (`--to`)

A config file can name more places: `annals configure --to team --target host:/path --base-url https://team.example.com/annals` saves a `[targets.team]` table and leaves the default alone. Then `annals publish r.md --to team` (also `ls`, `show`, `trash`, `restore`, `group`, `groups`) works on that place only, and `annals copy <link-or-id> --to team [--source other]` copies documents or whole groups there, keeping their ids. Nothing about the place is in the code: a name, a target and a base url.

## Hosting the page

**Inside an app platform** (the usual case). Mount the API under the platform’s prefix and let the platform’s login gate it:

```python
# server.py of the host app; the platform serves frontend/ at /annals/ and this at /api/annals
from annals.api import mk_api
app = mk_api(data_dir="/root/.local/share/annals")
```

and write the page shell once as the app’s frontend:

```bash
annals page-shell --api /api/annals --base /annals > frontend/index.html
```

The shell only names those two paths; the page’s script and style load from the API, so upgrading the package upgrades the page. Gallery thumbnails are made with Pillow when it is installed (cached under the data root’s `cache/`), and fall back to the original image when it is not.

**Standalone**, for a machine with no platform:

```bash
pip install 'annals[server]'
ANNALS_DATA_DIR=~/.local/share/annals annals serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8765
```

The page is at `http://127.0.0.1:8765/annals/`, its API under `/annals/api/`. Auth is chosen by environment variables:

| Situation                                                 | Set                                                                                                   | Effect                                                                                                                        |
|-----------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Behind an existing login that exposes a who-am-I endpoint | `ANNALS_WHOAMI_URL`, `ANNALS_ALLOWED_USERS=me@example.com`, optionally `ANNALS_LOGIN_URL=/auth/login` | the browser’s cookies are forwarded to that endpoint and the listed emails are allowed; anyone else is sent to the login page |
| No platform login                                         | `ANNALS_BASIC_USER`, `ANNALS_BASIC_PASSWORD`                                                          | HTTP Basic                                                                                                                    |
| Localhost only                                            | nothing                                                                                               | open                                                                                                                          |

## Acting on documents: pick, then choose what you want back

On a group’s page, tick the documents you want (with none ticked, all of them count); a bar at the bottom says what is picked and offers three buttons named after what they give, each opening one sheet (Back closes it):

- **Links**: **One link** for a person (expiry, optional password, and on a document “What’s included”) or **A link per document** for a notebook (one plain page each, no password). Your own agents need neither: the sheet’s first line copies the private address, which they read with `annals aggregate <link>`. Every link has its own copy button, plus **Copy all**.
- **One file**: the picked documents’ files (Markdown, html, text, PDFs, images) as one Markdown, PDF or web page file, to copy, download or open.
- **Listen**: a spoken review (when the host offers them, see below). For several documents, **One review of all** (their text is put in one document, tagged `combined` and added to the group, and that document gets an ordinary review; the same documents at the same versions reuse it) or **One each** (makes only the missing or out-of-date ones).

A document’s page has the same three buttons, acting on that document, and both pages keep the rest (copy the text, downloads, open raw, move to bin) under **⋯ More**. Every link, password and code block on the page has the same copy button: it copies inside the tap and answers on itself with a check and “Copied”.

## Spoken overviews

A document’s page can offer a Listen button: a few minutes of speech about the document, played with its script in sync. It is off unless the host turns it on, because making one spends money.

```python
app = mk_api(overviews=True)  # the button, and POST /docs/{id}/overview
```

A worker on the same machine fulfils the requests. It runs a command you choose, which takes a text file and writes one HTML page, and publishes that page as a document of its own:

```bash
export ANNALS_OVERVIEW_COMMAND='hailing overview {source} --minutes {minutes} --no-publish --player-to {out}'
annals listen-work                 # fulfils what is queued, one at a time
annals listen <doc-id> --minutes 3 # asks for one from the command line, as the button does
```

Run `annals listen-work` from a timer, not from a watcher on the folder: finished request files stay there, so a watcher would keep waking it. A current overview is not made again unless forced, and at most 20 are started in any 24 hours (`ANNALS_OVERVIEW_DAILY_LIMIT`). `annals.overview` has the details.

## Audio: what you still have to listen to

The **Audio** tab lists every spoken overview (documents tagged `overview`), newest first, with a search box and a filter by what you have heard: **Not started**, **In progress**, **Done**. Each row shows how much of it you heard and how many times you heard it to the end, and has a **Mark done** button for one you heard elsewhere.

An overview you asked for that is not made yet is listed above them, under **Not made yet**: being made (the tab looks again every few seconds and moves it into the list when it is ready), or failed, with when it was last tried, the document’s date, why (behind **Why**) and a **Try again** button. A command that answers in JSON (as `claude -p --output-format json` does) has its reason read out of it, so you see the reason rather than the envelope. A failure stays there for a week, so an overview you asked for never silently fails to appear.

Progress is kept on the server, per reader (the login’s email; `owner` with no login), so it follows you from the phone to the tablet: an overview you stopped halfway picks up where you stopped, on any device, with **Start over** beside it. What counts:

- **heard**: the distinct seconds played, so a replayed minute counts once; at 95% it is done;
- **listens**: each play that reaches the end of audio heard almost whole (dragging to the end is not a listen), counted once however often the page reports it;
- **your mark**: Mark done (or not done) wins over both; Reset forgets the document.

An overview plays inside a sandboxed frame, so the page cannot see its audio directly: every served html page that may play media gets a small relay script (`annals.media`) that posts what the player itself says it played to the page around it, so a locked screen, seeking or 2× speed are counted right (opt out with `data-annals-media="off"` on `<html>` or `<body>`; share links never carry it). Plain audio files are tracked from their own player. Records are one JSON file per reader under the data root (`listening/<reader>.json`); `mk_api(listening=...)` takes any other store, and `listening=None` keeps none. Progress is recorded on the annals page itself; a page opened on its own (“Open full page”) does not report.

## Sharing one page

The annals is private; a **share link** lets someone without an account read ONE document (or one group) and nothing else. From the page, **Links › One link** on a document lists its files and the annals pages it links to under “What’s included”, so you choose what goes; from a shell:

```bash
annals share <id-or-link> --password -                       # 7 days by default; password from stdin
annals share <id> --expires 2026-11-30                       # or 12h, 30d, an ISO time, `never`
annals share <id> --include img/chart.png,img/map.png        # only these files (the page always goes)
annals shares                                                # live links (--all: revoked and expired too)
annals unshare <link-or-token>                               # off at once
```

The link is `<share_base_url>/<token>/`: 128 random bits, `noindex`, `no-referrer`. Every request is checked against the share’s record (`shares/<token>.json` under the data root), so a file you did not choose is a 404 even beside the shared page, a revoke or an expiry takes effect on the next request, and references to anything outside the share (an image you left out, a link to another annals page or to anything else on your annals’ host, an annals id in the text) are removed from every text file before it is sent (markdown, html, plain text, svg). A linked page you tick goes with the files it shows, not every file beside it. The password is a gate on the link, not an account: at least 8 characters, stored hashed (stdlib scrypt), with attempts limited per client and per link, and a correct one earns a cookie scoped to that link. Links are read-only and last 7 days unless you say otherwise.

Where the links are served:

- **Standalone** (`annals serve`): at `/annals/shared/<token>/`, outside the login, with nothing to configure.
- **Inside an app platform**: the share server must be reachable without the platform’s login, so run it as its own public app and tell annals where it is:

```python
# server.py of a second, PUBLIC app (the owner's app keeps its login)
from annals.share_api import mk_share_api
app = mk_share_api(data_dir="/root/.local/share/annals")
```

then set `ANNALS_SHARE_BASE_URL` (or `annals configure --share-base-url ...`, or `mk_api(share_base_url=...)` for the owner’s page) to that app’s public URL. Until it is set, shares are made but carry no link. `mk_share_api` takes `rate_limiter=` and `link_failure_limiter=` (anything with `allow(key) -> bool`, such as heed’s Redis limiter; the defaults count per process), `trusted_proxies=` (whose `X-Forwarded-For` names the client; loopback by default) and `private_hosts=`; the password `hasher` is a keyword of `annals.share.Shares` (argon2, or anything with `hash`/`verify`).

## Downloads

Every markdown page offers two downloads made by the server, under **One file** and under **⋯ More**: **Markdown (.md)** and a titled **PDF** with the images inside (audio, video and other files appear as a link to the resource). Both are named after the title (`quarterly-report-q3.pdf`) and are served under the same rules as the page: the owner’s login, or a share link’s scope (a recipient gets the filtered text and only the files the link includes). The PDF needs `pip install "annals[pdf]"` (WeasyPrint, which uses Pango; `annals[server]` includes it); without it the PDF action answers with that hint. Pages (`/d/<id>`) are drawn in the browser by `app.js`, so a page that gains an action gains it for every existing document.

## One file from many: Markdown, PDF or a web page

**One file** (on a group, a selection or one document) combines the picked documents’ files into a single file and lets you choose its format: **Markdown** (shown, with **Copy Markdown**, **Download .md** and **Open as text**), **PDF** (with a bookmark for each file) or a **Web page** (one self-contained `.html`). Audio and video cannot be part of a document; they are listed as left out, each with the reason, and so is a file that cannot be read (a damaged or password-protected PDF) while the others still go in. It is made on each request and never stored. A share link has the same button, built from the share’s filtered text and only the files it includes.

| input                                 | to Markdown                     | to web page / to PDF                                                                  |
|---------------------------------------|---------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| markdown                              | as it is                        | rendered, the document’s images inside                                                |
| html                                  | converted (needs `markdownify`) | its structure and words; scripts, styles, frames, forms and remote images are dropped |
| text (`.txt`, `.json`, `.csv`, code…) | a code block                    | a preformatted block                                                                  |
| PDF                                   | its text (a scan has none)      | web page: its text; PDF: its pages, joined as they are                                |
| image                                 | not supported                   | a figure / a page of its own                                                          |

An image or a text file that sits in a document with pages (markdown, html, a PDF) belongs to that document, not a section of its own: a report and its figures combine as the report. Files are arranged with numbered names first, in numeric order, then the rest in the documents’ order.

```bash
annals aggregate <group-or-doc-id-or-link> > all.md                    # Markdown, from a shell
annals aggregate <id> --format pdf --output all.pdf                     # a PDF needs --output
annals aggregate <id> --format html --output all.html
annals aggregate <id> --order given --demote 0 --no-toc --keep-wraps   # Markdown options
```

The libraries behind each pair load only when it is used: PDF pages need WeasyPrint (which uses Pango), joining and reading PDFs need `pypdf` and `pdfdol`, html to Markdown needs `markdownify`. `pip install "annals[pdf]"` installs them all; a missing one stops the job before it starts, naming the library and the command. The API is `GET /groups/<gid>/aggregate?format=md|html|pdf` and `GET /aggregate?doc=<id>&doc=<id>` (`&download=1` to save, `&demote=`), `GET /<token>/aggregate` on the share server, and `GET /combine/formats` for what can be made; the response carries `X-Annals-Sections` (files that went in) and `X-Annals-Skipped` (percent-encoded JSON: which were left out and why).

A new pair (say docx to PDF) is one function in `annals/combine.py`, and every surface above learns it:

```python
from annals.combine import register

@register("docx", "pdf", requires=("some_module",))
def docx_to_pdf(item, ctx):          # item.text(), item.data(), item.rel; return the part for the format
    ...
```

```python
from annals.aggregate import aggregate_markdown        # the text mechanism, no documents involved
aggregate_markdown({"notes.md": "# Notes", "01-intro.md": "Hello"}, title="Bundle", demote=1)
```

`aggregate_markdown` takes `(path, text)` pairs and knows nothing of annals: `order=` (`numbered_first` by default, `None` for the order given, or any `paths -> paths` callable), `demote=`, `unwrap=`, `toc=`. The Markdown file has the title, a table of contents, and one `##` section per file named after its path (`Report/01-intro.md`); each file’s headings go one level down and hard-wrapped lines are joined. Footnotes are renamed per file so they do not collide, and a code block a file leaves open is closed at the end of its section. Relative links and images keep their paths, so they do not resolve inside the combined Markdown.

## A group’s documents as separate notebook sources

To take a group into a notebook (NotebookLM, now Gemini Notebook) with each document as its own source, open the group, tick the documents (none ticked means all), tap **Links**, choose **A link per document** and how long the links work (1 day by default), and tap **Make N links**. You get one link per page, each with its own copy button; tap **Copy all N links**, then in the notebook choose Add source → Website and paste: the notebook makes one source of each link, named after the document.

The links are an ordinary share of just those documents (no password, since the notebook cannot type one): unguessable, filtered like every shared text, and revocable with **Turn these links off** or under the **Links** tab. The notebook keeps its own copy once a link is added, so turning the links off afterwards does not remove the sources. Each link is a plain web page with no script (`<share link>/source/<doc id>/<file>`); markdown is rendered on the server, images, audio and PDFs get no link (a notebook takes those only as uploads). Why links and not a zip or a download: `misc/docs/notebook-sources.md`.

The API: `GET /shares/<token>/sources` (the owner’s) or `GET <share link>/sources` (the recipient’s) lists `{title, url}` per page; `GET /groups/<gid>/aggregate?doc=<id>&doc=<id>` combines only those documents.

## Other folders, search, filters and tags

Name extra folders when you mount the API, and they appear beside the published documents, each in its own section (`/annals/s/<name>`) and in `/annals/all`:

```python
app = mk_api(data_dir="~/.local/share/annals", sources={"ledgers": "~/.local/share/crowsnest/ledger"})
```

or, with no code, `ANNALS_SOURCES="ledgers=~/.local/share/crowsnest/ledger"` (several: comma-separated). A folder is read in place and never written: its files are listed newest first with their age, markdown renders, html is framed, the rest shows by its kind, and a sub-folder’s files count as written by the sub-folder’s name. Hidden files and caches are skipped.

On every list:

- **Search** matches every word, case-insensitively, against titles, tags, sessions, excerpts and the full text of markdown and text files (on the server; the matching passage shows under the title).
- **Filters** are one button per family (source, kind, session, date, tag). Checked values within a family are alternatives (“any of”), families combine (“and”), the counts are what each choice would give now, and the active filters show as removable chips. The filters and the search are in the URL, so Back undoes a filter and a link reproduces the view.
- **Tags**: add or remove them on any item’s page; they save as you go. They are stored apart from the items, in one file under the data root (`tags/tags.json`), so a ledger is never touched; on a published document they replace the tags the publisher gave.

The API behind it: `GET /items?q=&source=&trash=` → `{data, total}`, `GET /items/<source>:<id>`, `PATCH /items/<source>:<id>` with `{"tags": [...]}`, `GET /tags`, `GET /sources`, and `GET /files/<source>/<path>` for a folder’s raw files. The page reaches items through [`@zodal/store-http`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@zodal/store-http)’s provider (vendored; rebuild with `misc/vendor/build.sh`).

## Python API

```python
from annals import DocStore, publish
meta = DocStore("~/.local/share/annals").publish("report.md", tags=["q3"])
publish(["report.md"], tags="q3")["url"]          # same, through the configured target
```

`annals.api.mk_api(...)` is the mountable API; `annals.api.mk_app(data_dir=..., authorizer=...)` the standalone app. Both take `sources=` (name → folder path, or any `annals.sources.Source`) and `tags=` (any `MutableMapping` from item key to tag list; default `JsonTagStore`). `annals.catalog.Catalog` is the facade they stand on: every source’s rows as one list, searched, with the owner’s tags.

## Design notes

Flat store with tags and groups, not a hierarchy: agents from many projects do not share one, and every placement decision costs tokens. A document is `docs/<id>/meta.json` plus its files; the bin is `trash/<id>/`; a group is `groups/<gid>.json`. Ids are `YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS-<slug>-<4 hex>`, so a listing is already in time order and a URL says what it points to. The transport is a seam (`annals.target`): local directory, ssh, and later an http ingest endpoint. More in `misc/docs/design.md`.

## Skills

```bash
gh skill install thorwhalen/annals annals-publish
```

The skill also ships inside the package at `annals/data/skills/annals-publish/`.

# _autosummary/annals.aggregate.html.md

# annals.aggregate

Many markdown files as ONE markdown document: a title, a table of contents, a section per file.

The mechanism is text in, text out. [`aggregate_markdown()`](_autosummary/annals.aggregate.html.md#annals.aggregate.aggregate_markdown) takes `(path, text)` pairs
and knows nothing of documents, groups or shares; its choices are keyword arguments with
working defaults:

```default
>>> print(aggregate_markdown(
...     {"notes.md": "# Notes\nOne line\nwrapped.", "01-intro.md": "Hello."},
...     title="Bundle"), end="")
# Bundle

**Contents**

- [01-intro.md](#01-intromd)
- [notes.md](#notesmd)

## 01-intro.md

Hello.

## notes.md

## Notes
One line wrapped.
```

- `order`: how the files are arranged; [`numbered_first()`](_autosummary/annals.aggregate.html.md#annals.aggregate.numbered_first) by default (paths whose
  parts start with a number first, numerically, the rest in the order given), `None`
  keeps the order given, or any `paths -> paths` callable.
- `demote`: how many levels each file’s own headings go down (`1`: a file’s `#`
  becomes `##`); `0` leaves them.
- `unwrap`: join hard-wrapped lines of a paragraph or list item into one line
  ([`unwrap_lines()`](_autosummary/annals.aggregate.html.md#annals.aggregate.unwrap_lines)); code, tables, quotes and html are left as they are.
- `toc`: the table of contents, as links to the sections’ GitHub-style anchors.

[`doc_markdown_files()`](_autosummary/annals.aggregate.html.md#annals.aggregate.doc_markdown_files) is the bridge from annals documents: it yields the pairs for a
set of documents and the files of each a caller may read, through a `read` callable, so
the owner’s API, the share server (which reads filtered text) and the CLI share it.
Nothing is stored: the document is made per request.

### Functions

| [`aggregate_markdown`](_autosummary/annals.aggregate.html.md#annals.aggregate.aggregate_markdown)(files, \*[, title, order, ...])   | One markdown document of `files` (`{path: text}` or `(path, text)` pairs).              |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`demote_headings`](_autosummary/annals.aggregate.html.md#annals.aggregate.demote_headings)(text[, levels, max_level])           | `text` with every heading `levels` deeper (at most `max_level`); code untouched.        |
| [`doc_markdown_files`](_autosummary/annals.aggregate.html.md#annals.aggregate.doc_markdown_files)(docs, \*, read[, ...])            | `(path, text)` for every markdown file of `docs` (`(meta, files)` pairs).               |
| [`heading_anchor`](_autosummary/annals.aggregate.html.md#annals.aggregate.heading_anchor)(text[, seen])                         | The id GitHub (and most renderers) give a heading; `seen` numbers repeats.              |
| [`numbered_first`](_autosummary/annals.aggregate.html.md#annals.aggregate.numbered_first)(paths)                                | `paths` with numbered ones first, compared part by part, the rest in their given order. |
| [`strip_front_matter`](_autosummary/annals.aggregate.html.md#annals.aggregate.strip_front_matter)(text)                             | `text` without a leading YAML front-matter block (`---` .                               |
| [`unique_paths`](_autosummary/annals.aggregate.html.md#annals.aggregate.unique_paths)(pairs)                                  | The pairs with repeated paths told apart: `a.md`, `a.md (2)`.                           |
| [`unwrap_lines`](_autosummary/annals.aggregate.html.md#annals.aggregate.unwrap_lines)(text)                                   | `text` with hard-wrapped paragraphs and list items joined into one line each.           |

### annals.aggregate.aggregate_markdown(files, \*, title='', order=<function numbered_first>, demote=1, unwrap=True, toc=True, section_level=2)

One markdown document of `files` (`{path: text}` or `(path, text)` pairs).

A `# title`, a table of contents, then one section per file, headed by its path,
with the file’s text below (front matter dropped, headings `demote`-d, lines
unwrapped); see the module docstring for each choice.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### annals.aggregate.demote_headings(text, levels=1, , max_level=6)

`text` with every heading `levels` deeper (at most `max_level`); code untouched.

Setext headings (a line underlined with `===` or `---`) become `#` headings.

```pycon
>>> print(demote_headings("# A\nB\n---\n```\n# code\n```"))
## A
### B
```

```text
# code
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### annals.aggregate.doc_markdown_files(docs, \*, read, max_bytes=None, skip=(<class 'KeyError'>, <class 'OSError'>, <class 'ValueError'>))

`(path, text)` for every markdown file of `docs` (`(meta, files)` pairs).

`files` are the files of that document the caller may read, and `read(doc_id,
rel)` reads one (the share server passes its filtered reader). A document whose one
markdown file is its page is named by that file; a folder, or a document with several
markdown files, by its title then the file (`Report/01-intro.md`). A file `read`
cannot read (one of `skip`) is left out; past `max_bytes` in all, [`TooLarge`](_autosummary/annals.aggregate.html.md#annals.aggregate.TooLarge).

* **Return type:**
  [`Iterator`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Iterator)[[`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]]

### annals.aggregate.heading_anchor(text, seen=None)

The id GitHub (and most renderers) give a heading; `seen` numbers repeats.

```pycon
>>> seen = {}
>>> heading_anchor("01-intro.md", seen), heading_anchor("01-intro.md", seen)
('01-intromd', '01-intromd-1')
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### annals.aggregate.numbered_first(paths)

`paths` with numbered ones first, compared part by part, the rest in their given order.

A part (a folder or file name) that starts with digits sorts by that number, before any
part that does not; parts without a number keep the order they first appeared in, so a
folder’s files stay together.

```pycon
>>> numbered_first(["b.md", "10-z.md", "a.md", "2-y.md", "r/02.md", "r/01.md"])
['2-y.md', '10-z.md', 'b.md', 'a.md', 'r/01.md', 'r/02.md']
```

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### annals.aggregate.strip_front_matter(text)

`text` without a leading YAML front-matter block (`---` … `---`).

It must start with a `key:` line, so a page that opens with a horizontal rule
keeps it.

```pycon
>>> strip_front_matter("---\ntitle: x\n---\n# Body")
'# Body'
>>> strip_front_matter("---\nIntro\n---\nbody")
'---\nIntro\n---\nbody'
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### annals.aggregate.unique_paths(pairs)

The pairs with repeated paths told apart: `a.md`, `a.md (2)`.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]]

### annals.aggregate.unwrap_lines(text)

`text` with hard-wrapped paragraphs and list items joined into one line each.

Only ordinary text lines are joined: headings, list markers, quotes, tables, html,
fenced or indented code, and a line ending in a hard break (two spaces or `\`)
keep their line breaks.

```pycon
>>> print(unwrap_lines("A long\nsentence.\n\n- item\n  goes on\n- next\n\n    code\n    more"))
A long sentence.

- item goes on
- next

    code
    more
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)


# _autosummary/annals.auth.html.md

# annals.auth

The auth seam: who may read the annals.

A annals is private by construction, so the server asks every request who is calling. The
answer comes from one of three `Authorizer` callables, chosen by [`authorizer_from_env()`](_autosummary/annals.auth.html.md#annals.auth.authorizer_from_env)
(or passed to `annals.api.mk_app()`):

* [`no_auth()`](_autosummary/annals.auth.html.md#annals.auth.no_auth): everyone is the owner. Right for `annals serve` bound to `127.0.0.1`,
  wrong anywhere else.
* [`CookieWhoami`](_autosummary/annals.auth.html.md#annals.auth.CookieWhoami): forward the request’s cookies to an identity endpoint that answers
  `{"email": ...}` (enlace_auth’s `/auth/whoami`), and allow the listed emails. This is
  how a annals sits behind an existing login without owning passwords: the login page, the
  session cookie and the logout belong to the platform; the annals only checks the allowlist.
  Env: `ANNALS_WHOAMI_URL`, `ANNALS_ALLOWED_USERS` (comma separated), `ANNALS_LOGIN_URL`.
* [`BasicAuth`](_autosummary/annals.auth.html.md#annals.auth.BasicAuth): one username and password (HTTP Basic). For a annals with no platform
  login in front of it. Env: `ANNALS_BASIC_USER`, `ANNALS_BASIC_PASSWORD`.

An authorizer returns the caller’s identity (a string) or `None`. The API turns `None`
into a 303 to the login page for a browser GET, and a 401 for anything else, mirroring
what enlace_auth does so the two are indistinguishable from the phone.

### Functions

| [`authorizer_from_env`](_autosummary/annals.auth.html.md#annals.auth.authorizer_from_env)([env])   | Pick the authorizer the environment describes; see the module docstring.   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`no_auth`](_autosummary/annals.auth.html.md#annals.auth.no_auth)(request)             | Everyone is `owner`.                                                       |

### Classes

|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

| [`RequestLike`](_autosummary/annals.auth.html.md#annals.auth.RequestLike)(\*args, \*\*kwargs)                    | The two things an authorizer reads from a request.                              |

# _autosummary/annals.catalog.html.md

# annals.catalog

The catalog: every source’s items as one list, with search and the owner’s tags.

[`Catalog`](_autosummary/annals.catalog.html.md#annals.catalog.Catalog) is the facade the HTTP API stands on. It combines named sources (see
[`annals.sources`](_autosummary/annals.sources.html.md#module-annals.sources)) and a tag store (see [`annals.tags`](_autosummary/annals.tags.html.md#module-annals.tags)):

* [`Catalog.rows()`](_autosummary/annals.catalog.html.md#annals.catalog.Catalog.rows) lists items newest first, across sources or within one, filtered by
  a full-text query (every word must appear in the title, tags, session, excerpt or full
  text; case-insensitive), each row with the owner’s tags overlaid and, when there is a
  query, a `snippet` of the text around the first match.
* [`Catalog.item()`](_autosummary/annals.catalog.html.md#annals.catalog.Catalog.item) is one item, [`Catalog.set_tags()`](_autosummary/annals.catalog.html.md#annals.catalog.Catalog.set_tags) replaces its tags (in the tag
  store, never in the item), [`Catalog.tag_counts()`](_autosummary/annals.catalog.html.md#annals.catalog.Catalog.tag_counts) lists every tag in use.

Facets (kind, session, date, tag) are not computed here: the page counts them over the rows
it received, so every toggle is instant and the counts are always the ones the current
query would give.

### Functions

| [`mk_catalog`](_autosummary/annals.catalog.html.md#annals.catalog.mk_catalog)(store, \*[, sources, tags])   | The published documents first, then the extra sources; the owner's tags beside them.   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### Classes

|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

# _autosummary/annals.combine.html.md

# annals.combine

Many files of many kinds as ONE document: a Markdown, html or PDF file.

The mechanism is a registry. A *converter* turns one file of one kind into a *part* of the
output format (markdown text, an html fragment, a PDF); a *joiner* puts the parts of a
format together (a table of contents and a section each; bookmarks and pages). Which pairs
exist is the table [`REGISTRY`](_autosummary/annals.combine.html.md#annals.combine.REGISTRY), filled by [`register()`](_autosummary/annals.combine.html.md#annals.combine.register):

```default
@register("pdf", "md", requires=("pdfdol",))
def pdf_to_md(item, ctx): ...
```

so a new pair (docx to pdf, say) is one decorated function, and the web page, the API and
the CLI all learn it from [`supported()`](_autosummary/annals.combine.html.md#annals.combine.supported) without a change.

What goes in:

```default
=========  ===========  =======================================================
input      to md        to html / to pdf
=========  ===========  =======================================================
md         as it is     rendered (images of the document inside)
html       converted    its text and structure (scripts and styles dropped)
text       a code block a preformatted block
pdf        its text     html: its text; pdf: its pages, joined as they are
image      -            a figure (html) / a page of its own (pdf)
=========  ===========  =======================================================
```

Audio, video and other files have no place in a document: they are reported as left out,
each with the reason, never silently dropped. A file that cannot be read (a damaged or
password-protected PDF) is left out the same way, and the others still go in.

An image or a text file that sits in a document with pages (markdown, html, a PDF) is part
of that document, not a section of its own: a report and its figures combine as the report.

Heavy libraries load only when a pair needs them (WeasyPrint for PDF pages, pypdf and pdfdol
to join and read PDFs, markdownify for html to markdown); a missing one is a
[`annals.requirements.MissingDependency`](_autosummary/annals.requirements.html.md#annals.requirements.MissingDependency) that says what to install, raised before any
work starts. Nothing is stored: the document is made per call.

```pycon
>>> combined = combine([_demo_source({"b.md": "# B\ntext", "a.md": "hello"})], "md", title="T")
>>> combined.sections, combined.ext
(2, 'md')
>>> print(combined.data.decode().splitlines()[0])
# T
```

| [`MAX_SKIPPED_LISTED`](_autosummary/annals.combine.html.md#annals.combine.MAX_SKIPPED_LISTED)  | skipped files listed in a result (and its headers); the rest are counted                                                                             |
| [`MAX_TEXT_PAGES`](_autosummary/annals.combine.html.md#annals.combine.MAX_TEXT_PAGES)      | a PDF with more pages than this is not read for its text (about 0.2 s a page)                                                                        |

#### read_bytes *: [Callable](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [bytes](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#bytes)] | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)* *= None*

### annals.combine.combine(sources, fmt='md', \*, title='', demote=1, toc=True, unwrap=True, order=<function numbered_first>, max_text_bytes=8000000, max_input_bytes=120000000, registry=None)

Every usable file of `sources` as one `fmt` (“md”, “html” or “pdf”) file.

`sources` are the documents ([`Source`](_autosummary/annals.combine.html.md#annals.combine.Source)), in their order; files are arranged by
`order` ([`annals.aggregate.numbered_first()`](_autosummary/annals.aggregate.html.md#annals.aggregate.numbered_first): numbered names first, numerically;
`None` keeps the documents’ order). `demote` is how far an embedded markdown file’s
headings go down in a markdown output, which also takes `toc` (a table of contents)
and `unwrap` (join hard-wrapped lines). `max_text_bytes` caps all the text read
([`annals.aggregate.TooLarge`](_autosummary/annals.aggregate.html.md#annals.aggregate.TooLarge)), `max_input_bytes` all the files together.

A file with no converter, or that cannot be read, is left out and listed in
`Combined.skipped` with the reason. Raises [`NothingToCombine`](_autosummary/annals.combine.html.md#annals.combine.NothingToCombine) when nothing is
left, [`annals.requirements.MissingDependency`](_autosummary/annals.requirements.html.md#annals.requirements.MissingDependency) when a library the conversions need
is not installed (before any work), and `ValueError` for an unknown `fmt`.

* **Return type:**
  [`Combined`](_autosummary/annals.combine.html.md#annals.combine.Combined)

### annals.combine.explain(fmt)

One sentence on what a `fmt` output is made of (the ‘supported’ part of a message).

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### annals.combine.html_body(text, \*, rewrite_src=<function <lambda>>, demote=0)

The content of an html page as a safe fragment: its structure and words, nothing live.

Only a fixed set of tags survives, with a few plain attributes: no script, style, frame,
form, event handler, `class` or `id`; a link keeps only an `http(s)` or `mailto`
address. `rewrite_src(src)` decides each image: the url to show it from, or `None`
for its alt text instead (an image is never loaded from where the page says). `demote`
pushes headings that many levels down. Unbalanced tags are closed, so a fragment can
never swallow what is joined after it.

```pycon
>>> html_body('<body><script>x()</script><h1 onclick="x()">Hi</h1><a href="javascript:x()">y</a></body>')
'<h1>Hi</h1><a>y</a>'
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### annals.combine.items_of(sources, fmt)

The files to try for a `fmt` output, in the documents’ order.

A document with pages (markdown, html, PDF) contributes those; its images and text
files are its own parts. A document with none contributes whatever it holds, so what
cannot be used (a video) is reported and not silently missing. A folder, or a document
with several such files, names each by its title then the file (`Report/01-intro.md`).

* **Return type:**
  [`Iterator`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Iterator)[[`Item`](_autosummary/annals.combine.html.md#annals.combine.Item)]

### annals.combine.kinds_for(fmt)

The kinds of file that can be put in a `fmt` output, in a stable order.

* **Return type:**
  [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis)]

### annals.combine.register(kind, fmt, , requires=())

Decorator: the function turns a file of `kind` into a part of the `fmt` output.

`requires` are the (importable) modules it needs, checked before any work starts.

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`Item`](_autosummary/annals.combine.html.md#annals.combine.Item), [`Context`](_autosummary/annals.combine.html.md#annals.combine.Context)], [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`bytes`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#bytes)]], [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`Item`](_autosummary/annals.combine.html.md#annals.combine.Item), [`Context`](_autosummary/annals.combine.html.md#annals.combine.Context)], [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`bytes`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#bytes)]]

### annals.combine.skipped_header(skipped)

The skipped files as compact JSON for a response header: few, short, ascii.

At most [`MAX_SKIPPED_LISTED`](_autosummary/annals.combine.html.md#annals.combine.MAX_SKIPPED_LISTED) are listed (the count says how many there were) and
names and reasons are cut, so the header stays far under what a proxy accepts.

* **Return type:**

What can be made: `{format: {"label", "ext", "kinds"}}`, for a page or a message.

# _autosummary/annals.config.html.md

# annals.config

Settings: where documents are published and what link to print.

Two values matter to a publisher:

* `target`: where the documents go. A directory (`~/.local/share/annals`) or an ssh
  destination (`tw:/root/.local/share/annals`). This is the data root the annals server
  reads, locally or on another machine.
* `base_url`: the public root of the annals app, so a publish can print the link the owner
  opens (`https://apps.example.com/annals`).
* `share_base_url`: where the public share server answers, so `annals share` prints the
  link a recipient opens (`<share_base_url>/<token>/`). It defaults to
  `<base_url>/shared`, which is where `annals serve` mounts it; a platform that runs the
  share server as its own public app sets it (`ANNALS_SHARE_BASE_URL` or the config file).

Resolution order, highest first: explicit keyword arguments, environment variables
(`ANNALS_TARGET`, `ANNALS_BASE_URL`), the config file (`$ANNALS_CONFIG` or
`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/annals/config.toml`, default `~/.config/annals/config.toml`), then the
local defaults (publish into the local data dir, link to a local `annals serve`).

Named targets (`--to NAME`): a second place to publish, opted into per command. The config
file holds them as `[targets.NAME]` tables with the same two keys; `annals configure --to
NAME --target ... --base-url ...` writes one. `to` picks it over the environment and the
file’s default, and explicit `target`/`base_url` arguments still win over `to`.

A third, `outbox`, is true for a target another machine pulls and empties (the server
fetches documents from it rather than being written to): a replacement published there
travels as it is and is applied where it lands (see [`annals.store`](_autosummary/annals.store.html.md#module-annals.store)). `ANNALS_OUTBOX`
overrides it.

The server side has two knobs of its own. `ANNALS_DATA_DIR` is the directory the API
reads. It defaults to `~/.local/share/annals`, which is also the default publish target,
so with no configuration at all `annals publish` and `annals serve` meet in the same
place. `ANNALS_SOURCES` names extra folders the page lists beside the published documents,
read in place (`ledgers=~/.local/share/crowsnest/ledger`; several, comma-separated).

### Module Attributes

| [`ENV_SHARE_BASE_URL`](_autosummary/annals.config.html.md#annals.config.ENV_SHARE_BASE_URL)   | where the public share server answers (a share link is `<this>/<token>/`)   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`ENV_SOURCES`](_autosummary/annals.config.html.md#annals.config.ENV_SOURCES)          | "name=path, name2=path2"                                                    |

### Functions

|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`default_data_dir`](_autosummary/annals.config.html.md#annals.config.default_data_dir)()                             | The local data root: `$ANNALS_DATA_DIR` or `~/.local/share/annals`.                |
| [`load_settings`](_autosummary/annals.config.html.md#annals.config.load_settings)(\*[, target, base_url, to, ...]) | Resolve settings: arguments, then `to`, env, the config file, then local defaults. |
| [`named_targets`](_autosummary/annals.config.html.md#annals.config.named_targets)(\*[, config_path])               | The `[targets.NAME]` tables of the config file: name -> {target, base_url}.        |
| [`write_config`](_autosummary/annals.config.html.md#annals.config.write_config)(settings, \*[, to, config_path])  | Write the config file (string keys only; no TOML writer dependency needed).        |

# _autosummary/annals.html.md

# annals

annals: an in-tray for AI agents. Publish documents and media to a private page; get a link.

Agents call [`annals.tools.publish()`](_autosummary/annals.tools.html.md#annals.tools.publish) (or `annals publish file.md` from a shell) and hand
the printed URL to their human, who opens it on a phone. The documents are plain files in a
directory, local or on another machine over ssh; `annals.api.mk_app()` serves that
directory as a private page with search, sort, groups and a recycle bin.

### Functions

| [`configure`](_autosummary/annals.html.md#annals.configure)(\*[, target, base_url, to, outbox, ...])   | Write the publisher config (where to publish, what link to print) and show it.                                                                                    |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`group`](_autosummary/annals.html.md#annals.group)(title, doc_ids, \*[, target, base_url, to])    | Make a group (one URL for a set of documents) from existing document ids.                                                                                         |
| [`groups`](_autosummary/annals.html.md#annals.groups)(\*[, target, base_url, to])                   | List groups, newest first.                                                                                                                                        |
| [`load_settings`](_autosummary/annals.html.md#annals.load_settings)(\*[, target, base_url, to, ...])       | Resolve settings: arguments, then `to`, env, the config file, then local defaults.                                                                                |
| [`ls`](_autosummary/annals.html.md#annals.ls)([q, trash, limit, target, base_url, to])          | List documents (newest first), optionally filtered by words or showing the bin.                                                                                   |
| [`parse_target`](_autosummary/annals.html.md#annals.parse_target)(spec)                                   | `host:/path` becomes an [`SshTarget`](_autosummary/annals.html.md#annals.SshTarget); anything else a [`LocalTarget`](_autosummary/annals.html.md#annals.LocalTarget). |
| [`publish`](_autosummary/annals.html.md#annals.publish)(paths, \*[, title, tags, group, ...])        | Publish one document and print its link; several paths become several documents.                                                                                  |
| [`restore`](_autosummary/annals.html.md#annals.restore)(doc_ids, \*[, target, to])                   | Bring documents back from the recycle bin.                                                                                                                        |
| [`show`](_autosummary/annals.html.md#annals.show)(doc_id, \*[, target, base_url, to])             | A document's metadata, link, and the groups it is in (`to`: on a named target).                                                                                   |
| [`trash`](_autosummary/annals.html.md#annals.trash)(doc_ids, \*[, target, to])                     | Move documents to the recycle bin (restorable).                                                                                                                   |

### Classes

| [`DocStore`](_autosummary/annals.html.md#annals.DocStore)(target, \*[, settle])                | Publish, list, read, trash, restore and group documents on a `Target`.      |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`LocalTarget`](_autosummary/annals.html.md#annals.LocalTarget)(root)                             | A directory on this machine.                                                |
| [`Settings`](_autosummary/annals.html.md#annals.Settings)(target, base_url[, configured, ...]) | Where to publish and what link to print.                                    |
| [`SshTarget`](_autosummary/annals.html.md#annals.SshTarget)(host, root)                         | `host:path` on another machine, via the system ssh and rsync in batch mode. |

One document’s meta; `in_trash` says which side of the bin it is on.

`<id>@<n>` is version `n`: its own meta, with `version_of` naming the document.
A pending replacement, read by its own id, says `pending`. `settle=False`

#### publish(\*sources, title=None, tags=(), source=None, text=None, filename='document.md', exclude=('.\*', '_\_pycache_\_', '\*.pyc', '\*.pyo'), replace=None, artifact=None)

Publish files (or a directory, or `text`) as ONE document; return its meta.

One markdown or html file is the common case. A directory is published whole, with
`index.html` (or the first renderable file) as the page shown. `text` publishes a
string as `filename` instead of reading sources. `exclude` lists glob patterns
skipped inside a directory (hidden files and caches by default; `()` keeps all).

`replace` (a document id) publishes a new version of that document instead of a
new document: same id, same link, the current files kept as a version. It is
written as a pending replacement and applied at once when this store settles
(otherwise where the store is read). The returned meta says `pending` until then.

`artifact` (a claude.ai artifact link, see `check_artifact_url()`) is the
interactive version of the page: the document’s page links out to it. A
replacement that names none keeps the document’s current one.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

Delete a document that is in the bin. Refuses one that is not.

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

#### restore(doc_id)

Move a document out of the bin (idempotent).

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

#### search(query, , trash=False)

Case-insensitive match of every query word against title, tags, excerpt, source.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](_autosummary/annals.html.md#annals.DocStore.list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

#### settle(doc_id=None)

Apply pending replacements (of one document, or all); return the ids replaced.

A replacement whose document is not here yet (it is still on its way, or the
document was purged) stays pending and is listed under its own id.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](_autosummary/annals.html.md#annals.DocStore.list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

#### trash(doc_id)

### annals.configure(, target=None, base_url=None, to=None, outbox=False, share_base_url=None)

Write the publisher config (where to publish, what link to print) and show it.

### Example

`annals configure --target tw:/root/.local/share/annals --base-url https://apps.example.com/annals`.
`--to NAME` saves the target and base url as a named target (`annals publish --to NAME`)
and leaves the default alone. `--outbox` marks the target as an outbox: a directory
the server pulls and empties (it cannot be written to from here), so replacements are
left for the server to apply; it is kept by later changes (`ANNALS_OUTBOX=0` or an
edit of the file turns it off). `--share-base-url` is where share links point when
the share server is not at `<base-url>/shared` (a platform running it as its own
public app). With no arguments, shows the resolved settings without writing.

### annals.publish(paths, , title=None, tags='', group=None, add_to=None, session=None, all_files=False, target=None, base_url=None, to=None, replace=None, artifact=None, no_link_check=False)

Publish one document and print its link; several paths become several documents.

`paths`: files of any kind (markdown, html, images, video, audio, pdf, text), a
directory (one document: an `index.html` or single page with its assets, else a
gallery of everything in it), or `-` for stdin (markdown). `tags` is comma separated. `group`
names a group to create from the published documents; the reply then carries
`group_url` too. `add_to` appends them to an existing group instead (its id, as
printed in a group link), so a second batch lands under the link the owner already has. `session` records who published (the source shown on the page). A directory skips
hidden files and caches (`.*`, `__pycache__`, `*.pyc`) unless `all_files`.
`to` publishes to a named target of the config file (`[targets.NAME]`, see
`annals configure --to`) instead of the default one. `replace` (a document’s link or
id) publishes ONE path as a new version of that document: the link stays the same, the
page shows the new version and offers the earlier ones. That is how a living page (a
guide, a status page) keeps one link. `artifact` (a claude.ai artifact link) is the
interactive version of the page: the document’s page shows an “Open the interactive
version” button. Publish the Artifact first, then the same page here with its link.
A markdown or text document that mentions an issue or a Slack/email/chat message
without linking to it gets a warning on stderr ([`annals.linkcheck`](_autosummary/annals.linkcheck.html.md#module-annals.linkcheck)); it is
published either way. `no_link_check` turns that check off.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

# _autosummary/annals.jsonstore.html.md

# annals.jsonstore

A `MutableMapping` kept in one JSON file, safe with several server processes.

The owner’s tags ([`annals.tags`](_autosummary/annals.tags.html.md#module-annals.tags)) and each reader’s listening progress
([`annals.listening`](_autosummary/annals.listening.html.md#module-annals.listening)) are small, server-side records that the page changes one entry at
a time. [`JsonFileStore`](_autosummary/annals.jsonstore.html.md#annals.jsonstore.JsonFileStore) is that one mechanism: a JSON object in a file, written
atomically under an exclusive `flock`, re-read whenever another process changed it, and
never broken by a damaged file (it reads as empty and is kept aside at the next write).

A subclass says what a valid value is ([`JsonFileStore.valid()`](_autosummary/annals.jsonstore.html.md#annals.jsonstore.JsonFileStore.valid)) and how a value is
cleaned before it is stored ([`JsonFileStore.clean()`](_autosummary/annals.jsonstore.html.md#annals.jsonstore.JsonFileStore.clean)). [`JsonFileStore.modify()`](_autosummary/annals.jsonstore.html.md#annals.jsonstore.JsonFileStore.modify)
changes one entry from its current value under the lock, so two devices reporting at once
never lose each other’s change.

```pycon
>>> import tempfile, pathlib
>>> s = JsonFileStore(pathlib.Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) / "x.json")
>>> s["a"] = {"n": 1}
>>> s.modify("a", lambda v: {"n": (v or {}).get("n", 0) + 1})
{'n': 2}
>>> dict(s)
{'a': {'n': 2}}
```

### Module Attributes

| [`DAMAGED_SUFFIX`](_autosummary/annals.jsonstore.html.md#annals.jsonstore.DAMAGED_SUFFIX)   | the suffix a damaged file is kept under, so a hand edit gone wrong can be recovered   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### Classes

| [`JsonFileStore`](_autosummary/annals.jsonstore.html.md#annals.jsonstore.JsonFileStore)(path)   | `{key: value}` in one JSON file, re-read when another process changed it.   |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### annals.jsonstore.DAMAGED_SUFFIX *= '.damaged'*

the suffix a damaged file is kept under, so a hand edit gone wrong can be recovered

### *class* annals.jsonstore.JsonFileStore(path)

Bases: [`MutableMapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.MutableMapping)

`{key: value}` in one JSON file, re-read when another process changed it.

A write takes an exclusive `flock` on `<file>.lock`, re-reads the file, changes it
and replaces it atomically. A read re-reads the file whenever its inode, size or mtime
changed (every write makes a new inode). `label` names the store in log messages.

#### clean(value)

The value as stored; raise `ValueError` to refuse it.

* **Return type:**
  [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)

#### modify(key, change)

Set `key` to `change(current value or None)`, atomically; returns the stored value.

`change` returning `None` deletes the entry (and returns `None`).

* **Return type:**
  [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)

#### snapshot()

Every entry at once, under one read (what a listing overlays).

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]

#### valid(value)

Whether a value read from the file is kept (an invalid one is logged and skipped).

* **Return type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)


# _autosummary/annals.linkcheck.html.md

# annals.linkcheck

Find what a document mentions without linking to it: the owner reads on a phone and clicks through.

A published report says “Karl asked on 10-29 in #tech-app-test” or “see owner/repo#12”.
Without a link the reader has to go and find the message or the issue, often on a phone.
This module finds such mentions so `annals publish` can warn the author. It only warns
and never blocks: the author decides.

Two kinds, both in markdown or plain text (code spans and fenced blocks are ignored):

- `issue`: a GitHub-style reference, `owner/repo#12` or a bare `#12`, outside a link;
- `message`: a line that points at one message (a message, a thread, a DM, a reply, a
  post, someone who asked, said or wrote, or a `#channel`), carries a date, and has no
  web address at all. A dated pointer to a conversation names one message, so it should be
  its permalink. Headings and date ranges (“2026-10-04 → 2026-11-07”) are periods, not
  messages, and are skipped.

```pycon
>>> doc = '''# Catch-up
... - Karl asked on 2026-10-29 in #tech-app-test what was missing.
... - Karl asked on [2026-10-29](https://x.slack.com/archives/C1/p1) in #tech-app-test.
... - Tracked in inoocq/meta#7 and #12.
... - Tracked in [inoocq/meta#7](https://github.com/inoocq/meta/issues/7).
... - Run `git log #3` here.
... ## Slack, 2026-10-04 → 2026-11-07
... - 574 messages from 2026-10-04 to 2026-11-07, Slack read by hand until 10-04.
... '''
>>> [(m.line, m.kind, m.ref) for m in unlinked_mentions(doc)]
[(2, 'message', 'Slack/chat message of 2026-10-29'), (4, 'issue', 'inoocq/meta#7'), (4, 'issue', '#12')]
```

# _autosummary/annals.listening.html.md

# annals.listening

What each reader has heard of each audio document: percent heard, listens, where they stopped.

The page reports what was played, a few seconds at a time, as spans of the audio’s own
timeline (`[[start, end], ...]` in seconds). The server keeps the **union** of those spans
per reader and document, so the percent heard counts each second once, however often it was
replayed or skipped back to, and two devices reporting the same minute add nothing twice.
A listen is counted when playback reaches the end of audio that has been heard almost
whole ([`DONE_SHARE`](_autosummary/annals.listening.html.md#annals.listening.DONE_SHARE)), so dragging to the end is not a listen; a report carries the
id of the play it belongs to, so a report sent twice (a retry, a page closing) counts one.

A record, per reader and document:

```default
{"heard": [[0.0, 61.5], [90.0, 120.0]], "duration": 300.0, "position": 120.0,
 "listens": 1, "done": true, "updated": "2026-11-09T10:00:00+00:00"}
```

`done` is the reader’s own mark (“I have heard this”), set or cleared from the page; it
is absent until they set it. [`status()`](_autosummary/annals.listening.html.md#annals.listening.status) reads a record as one of [`STATUSES`](_autosummary/annals.listening.html.md#annals.listening.STATUSES).

Records live under the data root, one JSON file per reader (`listening/<reader>.json`),
through [`annals.jsonstore.JsonFileStore`](_autosummary/annals.jsonstore.html.md#annals.jsonstore.JsonFileStore). [`for_reader()`](_autosummary/annals.listening.html.md#annals.listening.for_reader) is the seam: any
`(reader) -> store` callable whose stores are [`Records`](_autosummary/annals.listening.html.md#annals.listening.Records) can replace it
(`mk_api(listening=...)`).

```pycon
>>> merge_spans([[5, 10], [0, 3], [2, 6], [20, 20]])
[[0.0, 10.0]]
>>> rec = apply_report(None, {"spans": [[0, 30]], "duration": 100, "position": 30})
>>> percent(rec), status(rec)
(30, 'started')
>>> apply_report(None, {"spans": [[95, 100]], "duration": 100, "ended": "p0"})["listens"]  # dragged to the end
0
>>> rec = apply_report(rec, {"spans": [[30, 100]], "duration": 100, "position": 100, "ended": "p1"})
>>> rec = apply_report(rec, {"spans": [], "duration": 100, "position": 100, "ended": "p1"})
>>> percent(rec), rec["listens"], status(rec)
(100, 1, 'done')
```

### Module Attributes

| [`STATUSES`](_autosummary/annals.listening.html.md#annals.listening.STATUSES)         | what a record reads as, in the order the page offers them as filters               |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`DONE_SHARE`](_autosummary/annals.listening.html.md#annals.listening.DONE_SHARE)       | heard at least this share of the audio counts as done, without a listen to the end |
| [`MIN_STARTED_S`](_autosummary/annals.listening.html.md#annals.listening.MIN_STARTED_S)    | heard less than this many seconds is not started (a stray tap on play)             |
| [`MAX_SPANS`](_autosummary/annals.listening.html.md#annals.listening.MAX_SPANS)        | at most this many separate spans are kept; past it the closest ones are joined     |
| [`MAX_REPORT_SPANS`](_autosummary/annals.listening.html.md#annals.listening.MAX_REPORT_SPANS) | a report holds at most this many spans                                             |
| [`MAX_DURATION_S`](_autosummary/annals.listening.html.md#annals.listening.MAX_DURATION_S)   | longest audio a report may claim, in seconds (a sanity bound, not a feature limit) |
| [`RECENT_PLAYS`](_autosummary/annals.listening.html.md#annals.listening.RECENT_PLAYS)     | the plays that reached the end, remembered so a retried report counts none twice   |

# _autosummary/annals.media.html.md

# annals.media

The media relay for published html pages: what a framed page plays, told to the page around it.

A spoken overview is an html page shown in a sandboxed frame, so the annals page cannot see
its audio. This adds one inlined script (the page’s own `ui/media-progress.js`) to any
html page that may play audio or video; the script posts what is played to the parent
page, which records what the reader heard ([`annals.listening`](_autosummary/annals.listening.html.md#module-annals.listening)), and takes a “start at”
from it. Opened on its own (no parent), the script does nothing.

### Functions

| [`add_media_relay`](_autosummary/annals.media.html.md#annals.media.add_media_relay)(html)   | `html` with the media relay injected, unless it plays nothing or opts out.                                          |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`media_version`](_autosummary/annals.media.html.md#annals.media.media_version)()         | A short hash of what [`add_media_relay()`](_autosummary/annals.media.html.md#annals.media.add_media_relay) injects, for a page's ETag. |

### annals.media.add_media_relay(html)

`html` with the media relay injected, unless it plays nothing or opts out.

```pycon
>>> add_media_relay(b"<p>no media</p>") == b"<p>no media</p>"
True
>>> b"annalsMedia" in add_media_relay(b"<body><audio src=a.mp3></audio></body>")
True
>>> add_media_relay(b"<p>an audio overview</p>") == b"<p>an audio overview</p>"
True
```

* **Return type:**
  [`bytes`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#bytes)

### annals.media.media_version()

A short hash of what [`add_media_relay()`](_autosummary/annals.media.html.md#annals.media.add_media_relay) injects, for a page’s ETag.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)


# _autosummary/annals.notebook.html.md

# annals.notebook

A share’s documents as separate notebook sources: one plain web page per text file.

A notebook product (NotebookLM, and Gemini’s notebooks, which share its sources) takes a
web page by its link, one source per link, and several links pasted at once; it reads
the page’s text and keeps its own copy. It does not unpack a zip, and its upload picker
needs the files on the device first. So the fewest taps from an iPad is: tick the
documents, copy one list of links, paste it into the notebook (see
`misc/docs/notebook-sources.md` for the research behind this).

The links are a share’s ([`annals.share`](_autosummary/annals.share.html.md#module-annals.share)): unguessable, scoped to the documents
ticked, expiring, revocable, and filtered like every shared text. This module only
decides what becomes a source and how one looks:

```default
GET <share link>/source/<doc id>/<file>   a script-free html page: <title>, the text
```

- [`source_files()`](_autosummary/annals.notebook.html.md#annals.notebook.source_files): which files of a document are sources (markdown and html pages,
  numbered files first, as [`annals.aggregate.numbered_first()`](_autosummary/annals.aggregate.html.md#annals.aggregate.numbered_first) orders them).
- [`notebook_sources()`](_autosummary/annals.notebook.html.md#annals.notebook.notebook_sources): the `{doc, file, title, url}` rows of a share, in its order.
- [`source_scope()`](_autosummary/annals.notebook.html.md#annals.notebook.source_scope): what a notebook share includes of a document: its source pages
  and the files they show, never the rest of a folder.
- [`render_source()`](_autosummary/annals.notebook.html.md#annals.notebook.render_source): one markdown file as its source page, shared-text rules applied
  twice: to the text ([`annals.share.filter_refs()`](_autosummary/annals.share.html.md#annals.share.filter_refs)), then to every link and image of
  the rendered page ([`annals.share.ref_decider()`](_autosummary/annals.share.html.md#annals.share.ref_decider) over markdown-it’s tokens), and
  any annals id left in it removed. Cached, and rendered only up to
  [`RENDER_MAX_BYTES`](_autosummary/annals.notebook.html.md#annals.notebook.RENDER_MAX_BYTES) (a larger file is sent as escaped text): it is a public route.
- [`source_page()`](_autosummary/annals.notebook.html.md#annals.notebook.source_page): the page a notebook reads. Its `<title>` is the document’s title,
  which the notebook shows as the source’s name, so the sources can be told apart.
- [`markdown_html()`](_autosummary/annals.notebook.html.md#annals.notebook.markdown_html): markdown to html; `markdown-it-py` when installed (the
  `pdf` extra), else the text escaped in a `<pre>`, which a notebook reads as well.

### Module Attributes

| [`SOURCE_KINDS`](_autosummary/annals.notebook.html.md#annals.notebook.SOURCE_KINDS)      | the kinds of file a notebook can take from a link (images, audio, video and pdf it takes only as uploads)         |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

| [`SOURCE_CSP`](_autosummary/annals.notebook.html.md#annals.notebook.SOURCE_CSP)        | ones), nothing else; a sandbox (no origin, no script, no form) even so, since it is served beside the owner's app |
| [`HTML_SOURCE_CSP`](_autosummary/annals.notebook.html.md#annals.notebook.HTML_SOURCE_CSP)   | its own styles and images, no script, no request elsewhere                                                        |
| [`RENDER_MAX_BYTES`](_autosummary/annals.notebook.html.md#annals.notebook.RENDER_MAX_BYTES)  | rendering is superlinear on hostile input, and the route is public                                                |
| [`SOURCE_CACHE_SIZE`](_autosummary/annals.notebook.html.md#annals.notebook.SOURCE_CACHE_SIZE) | rendered source pages kept in memory (each at most a few times RENDER_MAX_BYTES)                                  |
